questions.prompt: In `DeadlockDemo`, `t1` runs `lock (lockA) { ... lock (lockB) ... }` and `t2` runs `lock (lockB) { ... lock (lockA) ... }`. Why can the program hang forever?
options: `Thread.Sleep(100)` inside a `lock` is not allowed and freezes the thread
Each thread holds its first lock while waiting for the lock the other holds
`Join()` is called before the threads have started
Two `lock` statements can never be nested in C#
questions.explanation: `t1` locks `lockA` then waits for `lockB`, while `t2` locks `lockB` then waits for `lockA`; neither releases its first lock, so both wait permanently. The fix is a consistent lock order.

questions.prompt: What does replacing `lock` with `Monitor.TryEnter(lockA, 1000)` give you?
options: It acquires both locks atomically, so ordering no longer matters
It makes the lock reentrant across threads
It gives up after the timeout, so the thread can handle it instead of waiting permanently
It releases the lock automatically after one second of work
questions.explanation: `Monitor.TryEnter` with a timeout returns `false` if the lock isn't acquired in time, so the code can handle the timeout and avoid a permanent wait; acquired locks are released in `finally`.

source.section: #### Fix 2 — use `Monitor.TryEnter` with timeout (avoid permanent wait)

questions.prompt: Ten threads each run `counter++` 100,000 times on a shared `static int counter`, with no locking. Why is the final value usually less than 1,000,000?
options: `counter++` is not atomic, so concurrent updates overwrite each other and increments are lost
`int` overflows before it reaches 1,000,000
`Join()` stops some threads before they finish their loops
Each thread works on its own copy of a `static` field
questions.explanation: This is a race condition: several threads modify shared data concurrently and `counter++` is not atomic, so updates are lost.

questions.prompt: For a simple shared counter, which fix does the lesson call fast and atomic?
options: Marking the loop body with `Thread.Sleep(0)`
Starting each thread with `IsBackground = true`
Calling `Monitor.TryEnter` without a timeout
`Interlocked.Increment(ref counter)`
questions.explanation: Fix B, `Interlocked`, is described as fast and atomic and best for simple atomic operations; Fix A wraps `counter++` in a `lock`.

questions.prompt: A WPF method calls `GetDataAsync().Result` on the UI thread and hangs. What is the first fix the lesson gives?
options: Call `.Wait()` instead of `.Result`
Don't block: `await GetDataAsync()` all the way up
Run the method inside `lock (this)`
Increase the `Task.Delay` so the UI thread finishes first
questions.explanation: `.Result` blocks the UI thread while the continuation tries to resume on that same captured context. The fix is not to block and use `await` all the way; library code can also use `ConfigureAwait(false)`.
